prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the layout of a covered walkway bordered on the left by a near vertical wall and glass storefront (0.5 to 3 metres away), an overhead ceiling plane with a smooth dark-to-bright gradient from front to back, and a wide plaza opening Ahead with a pillar and storefront booths on the right (5 to 12 metres away). A companion in the lower-left foreground (cropped below the shoulders) stays within arm's reach at roughly 0.5 to 1 metre from the camera wearer across frames 1 to 4 before dropping out of view in frame 5, while another pedestrian in a black hoodie on the right approaches from about 2.5 metres in frame 1 to within 1.5 metres in frame 2 before exiting the right edge. Further ahead, a woman in pink trousers walks away from roughly 3 metres in frame 1 to 7 metres in frame 5 toward a group of people spaced 0.5 to 2 metres apart at a distance of 5 to 8 metres, while another person in red and blue jeans approaches on the right from 8 metres down to about 3.5 metres by frame 5. This map clarifies the continuous ground-plane recession, the exact depth ordering of overlapping pedestrians, and the close proximity of the left-hand storefront pillar as the camera wearer walks past it in frames 2 to 4, which are harder to judge from the busy RGB lighting alone. However, the depth map is unreliable on the reflective glass wall on the left (treating reflections and interior space as a flat opaque surface), loses fine limb detail on distant pedestrians beyond 8 metres, and assigns a nearly uniform black value to the open background sky and distant buildings.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates roughly 10 to 13 individual pedestrians per frame distributed horizontally across the lower half of the scene, separating foreground people at 0.5 to 3 metres from mid-ground and background clusters at 4 to 12 metres, though it omits all architectural layout such as the floor, ceiling, walls, and pillars. In the lower-left foreground, the person within arm's reach (0.5 to 1 metre away, cropped at the chest/head) is segmented through frame 4 before disappearing in frame 5, while the person in the black hoodie on the right is segmented at 1.5 to 2.5 metres in frames 1 and 2 before leaving the frame, and the walking figure in pink trousers is tracked moving away from the centre foreground toward the mid-ground left group across frames 1 to 5. In the mid-ground (4 to 8 metres away), tightly spaced pedestrians standing within 0.5 to 1.5 metres of each other near the central walkway and right-hand green booth are segmented into distinct overlapping coloured masks, showing who partially occludes whom as the camera wearer advances and turns slightly right. Compared to the RGB strip, the segmentation masks make it much easier to count and individuate darkly dressed or overlapping people against the cluttered, dimly lit background and string lights. However, the map exhibits clear unreliability in class labels and temporal consistency: it misclassifies a background overhead structure as a 'bus' in frame 1, labels part of a person's torso as a 'backpack' in frame 4, mislabels an upper-right wall/sign area as a 'tv' in frame 5, and flickers or merges masks among the densely packed crowd on the right.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely empty, detecting only a single yellow body skeleton across frames 2 through 5 corresponding to the pedestrian in pink trousers and a dark top walking away in the left-centre of the walkway, while failing to detect any skeletons in frame 1 or for any of the other 10+ people in the scene. Across frames 2 to 5, this tracked skeleton shrinks and shifts upward in the image plane as the person retreats from roughly 3.5 metres to 7 metres in front of the camera wearer, moving from the central foreground toward the group standing 5 to 7 metres away on the left. The arrangement of the shoulder, hip, and leg keypoints indicates the person is upright and facing away from the camera wearer (walking toward the background), with their head turned slightly to the left in frame 2 and their legs scissoring as they stride forward and come within arm's reach of the two people standing in the left mid-ground by frame 5. The skeleton provides an explicit geometric readout of this pedestrian's torso orientation and walking gait in frames 2 to 5 stripped of visual clutter, though no magenta hand skeletons are resolved at this distance. The pose map is highly unreliable overall for scene understanding here, as it completely misses the camera wearer's close companion at 0.5 to 1 metre on the lower left (due to severe lower-body cropping), misses the approaching foreground pedestrian on the right in frames 1–2 and frame 5, and misses all other mid-ground and background people.
